paper.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.LG), v1 9 Oct 2026; code github.com/arareddy/mufsc
paper.one_liner: Exact same-seed replay unlearning for federated socially fair k-means, using per-(client, group) summaries that stay valid when global group weights change.
paper.summary: Hospitals or banks may want to cluster their records together without pooling them (federated clustering). They may also want the centers to serve every demographic group comparably well, and they must be able to delete records on request. This paper uses socially fair k-means: minimize the larger of the two groups' average squared distance to the nearest center. Under this objective a deletion is global, because removing a group-g record changes the group size n_g and so the weight 1/n_g of every group-g record at every institution. The authors fix the issue by having each (client, group) slice build its own k-means++ (D^2-sampling) summary with no reference to global group sizes. Only the server divides counts by n_g. A deletion therefore leaves summaries at untouched institutions valid. Initial centers are then refined with a guarded Fair-Lloyd update computed from exact integer count, sum and squared-sum statistics. Unlearning replays the fully specified training map with the same seed: it reuses untouched summaries, recomputes touched ones, and patches statistics exactly, so the output equals retraining bit for bit. For two groups they prove an O(log^2 k) initialization guarantee that does not depend on client group proportions. Whole-client withdrawal is up to 35.8x faster than retraining at zero refinement rounds. Single-record deletions save only about 6%.
paper.problem: Federated clustering systems should both represent demographic groups fairly and honor exact data deletion (e.g., GDPR erasure). Under socially fair k-means each record of group g has weight 1/n_g, so deleting a record at one site changes the normalization of every site's records, can alter initial centers and later fair updates, and simple subtraction from cached cluster statistics does not reproduce retraining. The open question is which parts of a federated fair-clustering computation can be kept after a deletion while the released model stays exactly what retraining would produce, and when keeping them actually saves work.
paper.core_idea: Separate local summary construction from everything that depends on global group sizes. Each (client, group) ownership slice selects up to k representatives by D^2-sampling on its own keyed random stream and reports multiplicities, never using n_g, so only the server's weights h/n_g change after a deletion elsewhere. Combined with a fully specified ('declared') deterministic training map, exact integer sufficient statistics and per-entity seeded streams, same-seed replay can reuse untouched work and patch the rest so that it reproduces retraining's entire indexed center trajectory.
paper.setting: Horizontal federated (cross-silo) unsupervised k-means clustering with C institutions holding disjoint records, each record having a binary protected group (e.g., census SEX); socially fair (minimax group-average cost) objective; exact unlearning of record batches and whole clients; simulated locally on one machine.
contributions: Group-separated federated initialization SplitGroup-2k: per-(client, group) D^2-sampling summaries, reweighted by h/n_g only at the server, with an expected O(log^2 k) socially-fair approximation factor (plus a quantization term) independent of n, C, group imbalance and client group proportions under ideal sampling (Theorem 1).

A tight negative result for the natural locally balanced single-summary adaptation of MUFC (Merged-1k): expected loss Theta(kappa), linear in the local/global group-share mismatch kappa (Theorem 2), plus a matched-slot gap for Merged-2k that one fair refinement round removes (Proposition 7).

A guarded, finite, deterministic version of the Fair-Lloyd two-group center update driven by exact (N, S, SS) statistics, which equals the centralized update (Prop 6) and never increases the worst-group cost (Prop 3).

Exact batch replay (Algorithm 1) with exact integer patching and assignment certificates (all-competitor Lemma 4 and stronger O(1) runner-up certificate, Prop 8), proven to reproduce same-seed retraining's whole indexed center trajectory (Theorem 5); 810/810 replay comparisons matched retraining exactly.

Cost analysis showing where reuse pays off and where it fails: a work bound (Eq. 29), a conditional locally-stable replay bound (Prop 9), and a scoped obstruction where one legal deletion forces Omega(n) expected duplicated assignment work for the specified sampler/cache/fallback policy (Lemma 10, Prop 11).

Empirical mapping on Adult, Bank, Credit and 2018 ACS census data: whole-client deletion 35.8x faster than retraining at T=0 and 2.4x/1.7x at T=1/2, but only about 1.06x for record deletion, with certification increasing aggregate end-to-end cost.

Extensions: raw-data-free compact whole-client replay state (Prop 13, following Pan et al. 2023 Sec 5.3), multi-group (m>2) bounds and a Frank-Wolfe dual prototype (Appendices B.4, G, L), and Lean 4 proofs of several mathematical results.
method_steps: Fix preprocessing once: clip and encode every feature on a fixed-point grid x = m * 2^-b (b = 12 in experiments); give records persistent identities; derive a separate PCG64 random stream for each (seed, role, client, group) slice and for the server (keyed random streams). Use an exact rational categorical sampler with fixed tie, saturation and zero-potential completion rules (the 'declared training map').

Phase I, local (per ownership slice e = (c, g), i.e. the group-g records of client c): select k_e = min(k, |X_e|) representatives by D^2-sampling (k-means++ seeding, no Lloyd steps) using the slice's own stream. Assign every slice record to its nearest representative to get multiplicities h_{e,j}. Snap representatives to a grid of width gamma to get anchors q_{e,j}. Send (q_{e,j}, h_{e,j}), at most 2k anchors per client. No global group size is used.

Phase I, server: compute global group sizes n_A, n_B exactly. Weight each anchor by omega_{e,j} = h_{e,j}/n_g, the only step that uses global sizes. Select k initial centers by exact weighted D^2-sampling on the server stream. Optionally run T_a deterministic weighted anchor-Lloyd iterations that never increase the weighted anchor objective.

Phase II, each of T rounds: the server broadcasts the indexed centers. Each client assigns every record to its nearest center (exact squared-distance comparisons, smallest-index ties). For every group-cell (group g, cluster j) the client computes exact integer statistics N_{g,j} (count), S_{g,j} (vector sum) and SS_{g,j} (squared-norm sum), and these are exactly aggregated; secure aggregation is not implemented. Clients cache each point's label, nearest and second-nearest distances, and runner-up center ID.

Server GuardedFairUpdate_L: from the statistics form group means mu_{g,j} and masses alpha_j = N_{A,j}/n_A, beta_j = N_{B,j}/n_B. For two-group clusters the candidate is c_j(lambda) = (lambda alpha_j mu_{A,j} + (1-lambda) beta_j mu_{B,j}) / (lambda alpha_j + (1-lambda) beta_j); a single-group cluster uses its group mean; an empty cluster keeps its old center. Evaluate lambda = 0, 1 and L bisection midpoints, scoring each rounded candidate exactly. Pick the one with the lowest max(f_A, f_B), and accept it only if it does not exceed the current centers' cost.

Checkpoint for unlearning: (i) every slice's anchors and multiplicities; (ii) global group sizes and the server sampling state; (iii) indexed centers and exact aggregate statistics for every round; (iv) at clients, each point's cached label, d1, d2 and runner-up ID per round (about 64nT bytes in memory, 48nT serialized).

Unlearning a batch R (valid only if both groups stay nonempty): reuse the cached (q, h) of every slice with no deleted record. Rerun D^2-sampling, assignment and quantization on X_e minus R for touched slices, with their original streams. Recompute n_g and the weights h/n_g, then rerun the server's weighted D^2-sampling (and any anchor-Lloyd steps) from its original stream.

Replay each refinement round: broadcast the replay centers and the per-center shifts delta_m relative to the cached trajectory. Remove deleted records from their cached group-cells. Certify each surviving cached label with the all-competitor test delta_j + max_{m != j} delta_m < d2 - d1 or the runner-up test (Eq. 28), and exactly reassign every failure. Patch (N, S, SS) with signed exact integer corrections. If more than half of the attempted certificates fail, discard the round's patches, rebuild statistics from zero, and assign directly from then on. Apply the same GuardedFairUpdate_L.
Direct replay variant: keep the Phase-I reuse but reassign every retained record in every round with no certificates. This is the variant that wins most timing comparisons.

Whole-client withdrawal with T = 0 (compact path, Prop 13): store only per-client summaries, exact per-client group counts and server settings. Drop the departing clients' summaries, update n'_g, rebuild the anchor list with weights h/n'_g, and rerun the server sampler from its original stream. No raw records are needed. This mirrors MUFC's server-only retraining.
Output the indexed center trajectory and final centers. Replay marks its cache invalid, so any later record deletion must first rebuild the per-point cache (about (n-r)kT distance queries).

key_definitions.name: Socially fair k-means objective
key_definitions.plain: Compute each group's average squared distance to its nearest center and minimize the worse (larger) of these group averages; each group-g record effectively carries weight 1/n_g.
key_definitions.formal: Phi_g(C) = (1/n_g) * sum_{x: g(x)=g} min_j ||x - c_j||^2 ; Phi(C) = max_{g in {A,B}} Phi_g(C)

key_definitions.name: Balanced surrogate G
key_definitions.plain: Sum of the two group-average costs, used in proofs; within a factor 2 of Phi.
key_definitions.formal: G(C) = Phi_A(C) + Phi_B(C), Phi <= G <= 2 Phi

key_definitions.name: Ownership slice (pseudo-client)
key_definitions.plain: The records of one group held by one client; the unit that builds an independent local summary.
key_definitions.formal: e = (c, g), X_e = X_{c,g} = {x in X_c : g(x) = g}

key_definitions.name: Group-cell
key_definitions.plain: Records of group g currently assigned to center j; depends on the current assignment, unlike ownership slices which depend on who stores the record.

key_definitions.name: Anchor weight
key_definitions.plain: Server weight of a quantized representative: its multiplicity divided by its group's global size.

key_definitions.name: Local/global mismatch kappa
key_definitions.plain: Largest ratio, over mixed clients, between a client's shares of the two global groups; measures how much local group balancing distorts global weights (hospital example: 30% of A vs 3% of B gives 10).
key_definitions.formal: a_c = n_{c,A}/n_A, b_c = n_{c,B}/n_B, kappa = max{1, max_{c: a_c b_c > 0} max(a_c/b_c, b_c/a_c)}

key_definitions.name: Declared training map
key_definitions.plain: The fully specified randomized training procedure Train(X; s), including orderings, tie-breaking, empty clusters, degenerate sampling cases, numeric encoding and per-entity random streams, relative to which exactness is defined.

key_definitions.name: Exact (same-seed) unlearning
key_definitions.plain: After deleting batch R, the released model and its entire indexed center trajectory must equal what retraining on the retained data with the same seed would produce.
key_definitions.formal: pi(Unlearn(Train(X; s), R; s)) = pi(Train(X \ R; s)) for every seed s

key_definitions.name: Assignment certificate
key_definitions.plain: Sufficient condition that a point's cached nearest center is still uniquely nearest after centers move.
key_definitions.formal: delta_j + max_{m != j} delta_m < d2 - d1 (Lemma 4); runner-up: d1 + delta_j < min{|d2 - delta_r|, max(0, d2 - max_{m not in {j,r}} delta_m)}

key_definitions.name: Useful coverage
key_definitions.plain: Share of survivor point-rounds whose assignment work certification actually saved after fallback discards.

key_definitions.name: Valid deletion batch
key_definitions.plain: A request that leaves both demographic groups nonempty (otherwise h/n_g and Phi_g are undefined).

theory.name: Theorem 1 (Split-group warm start)
theory.statement_plain: At gamma = 0, SplitGroup-2k's initial centers satisfy E[Phi(C0)] <= 2 alpha_k (sqrt(alpha_k) + 2)^2 Phi*, with alpha_k = 5(ln k + 2) (Makarychev-Reddy-Shan k-means++ factor). That is an O(log^2 k) factor independent of n, C, group imbalance and client group proportions. For gamma > 0 an additive O(d gamma^2 log k) quantization term appears (Eqs 14-16). Non-increasing anchor-Lloyd steps preserve the bound.
theory.assumptions: Two groups, both nonempty; ideal independent random bits for every slice and the server; exact rational categorical sampling; deterministic degeneracy rules; grid error ||q - z||^2 <= d gamma^2/4 (binary64 rounding handled in App B.3).
theory.significance: Shows that group-separated summaries can be reused after deletions without losing proportion-independent initialization quality. The proof bounds local replacement error slice by slice (weights are constant within a slice) and composes it with server D^2-sampling using L2 Minkowski inequalities.

theory.name: Theorem 2 (Tight heterogeneity dependence for Merged-1k)
theory.statement_plain: The locally group-balanced single-summary adaptation of MUFC has expected G/G* = O(kappa log^2 k) at gamma = 0 (Eq 26: E G <= alpha_k((1+sqrt(alpha_k)) sqrt(kappa) + 1)^2 G*). Conversely, for every rational kappa >= 1 there is a two-client, two-group, 1-D, k = 1 instance (gamma = T_a = 0) where the expected ratio is at least kappa/2 for G and kappa/4 for Phi.
theory.assumptions: Same as Theorem 1; the lower bound is not claimed for T_a > 0, for Merged-2k, or for the refined model, and is specific to the declared merged sampler.
theory.significance: Explains why fairness weights must not be balanced locally: a nearly pure client's tiny minority gets half its local sampling probability, a loss linear in the mismatch.

theory.name: Proposition 3 (Monotonicity)
theory.statement_plain: One nearest-center assignment step followed by GuardedFairUpdate_L never increases the worst-group cost Phi.
theory.assumptions: Exact scoring of the represented (rounded) candidates; the guard compares against the current centers on the current partition.
theory.significance: Refinement is safe to iterate. Appendix A.4 shows that without the guard, finite bisection can increase the cost (d = k = 1, A = {-1, +1}, B = {3}: one bisection step gives cost 13/4 > 25/9).

theory.name: Proposition 6 (Algorithm-relative centralized equivalence)
theory.statement_plain: If federated aggregation returns exact (N, S, SS), the federated GuardedFairUpdate_L returns exactly the same indexed centers as a centralized implementation with the same partition, candidate order and deterministic arithmetic.
theory.assumptions: Exact additive statistics; equivalence is to the declared finite guarded solver, not to the exact convex optimum.
theory.significance: Federation costs no quality relative to the centralized fair update, which the replay-exactness induction relies on.

theory.name: Proposition 7 (Pre-refinement gap with matched anchor slots)
theory.statement_plain: On a three-location, two-client, 1-D, k = 1 instance where Merged-2k and SplitGroup-2k each send two anchor slots per client, the expected ratios are E G/G* = (kappa+5)/3 vs 2 and E Phi/Phi* = (kappa+8)/6 vs 3/2. One full-data guarded fair-refinement round maps any incumbent to the optimum.
theory.assumptions: Rational kappa >= 1; gamma = T_a = T = 0; ideal categorical bits.
theory.significance: Matching the communication budget does not close the initialization gap, but the gap is an initialization effect that refinement can remove.

theory.name: Lemma 4 (All-competitor certificate)
theory.statement_plain: A retained point's cached unique winner j stays uniquely nearest if delta_j + max_{m != j} delta_m < d2 - d1, where delta_m is the displacement of center m between the cached and replay trajectories. The maximum must range over all competitors, not only the old runner-up.
theory.assumptions: Cached exact (or outward-bounded) d1 < d2 and displacement norms; strict inequality; ambiguous cases go to exact assignment.
theory.significance: Lets replay skip reassignment for points far from decision boundaries, using the Elkan/Hamerly movement-bound idea between the original and replay trajectories.

theory.name: Proposition 8 (Tightness and runner-up certificate)
theory.statement_plain: Given only (j, d1, d2) and displacement radii, Lemma 4 is the strongest universally sound test (tight for k >= 3 with exact norms; for k = 2 the condition is d1 + delta_j < |d2 - delta_r|). With the cached runner-up identity r, the strictly stronger test d1 + delta_j < min{|d2 - delta_r|, max(0, d2 - D_{not j,r})} is still O(1) per point after precomputing the three largest shifts.
theory.assumptions: A cache that stores only the label, d1, d2 and runner-up ID.
theory.significance: The cache cannot do much better, and richer caches (e.g. Yinyang-style) would be needed for more coverage.

theory.name: Theorem 5 (Seeded exact batch model-output unlearning)
theory.statement_plain: For every fixed seed s, the projection of Unlearn(Train(X; s), R; s) onto the entire indexed center trajectory and final model equals that of Train(X \ R; s). For a fixed or seed-independent R they are also equal in distribution over s.
theory.assumptions: Exact additive sufficient statistics; deterministic center arithmetic, quantization, ties, empty-cluster and zero-potential rules; separate seeded streams per slice and server; sound certificate comparisons; valid batch (both groups nonempty). There is no guarantee for adaptively chosen requests or for equality of full caches/state.
theory.significance: Core exactness result. The proof matches the initializer (untouched slices have the same inputs and tapes), then inducts over rounds: signed exact corrections turn cached statistics into fresh retained statistics, and abandonment preserves the update.

theory.name: Replay work bound (Eq. 29)
theory.statement_plain: At unit arithmetic cost, scanning replay costs O(W0 + W_I + nT + CkdT + Ck log k T + (L+2)kdT + rdT + [sum_t F_t + (n-r)|T_dir|](kd + k log k)), where W0 is per-call setup (Omega(n) even at T = 0), W_I is touched-slice plus server re-initialization, F_t counts failed certificates, and T_dir indexes full direct rounds. For a uniformly random batch, the expected touched-slice mass is at most r * s_max (Eq 34).
theory.assumptions: Unit-cost arithmetic model; bit complexity of exact integers is excluded.
theory.significance: Shows that exactness alone does not save work: per-round survivor scans and setup remain, so savings come mainly from Phase-I reuse.

theory.name: Proposition 9 (Locally stable replay)
theory.statement_plain: Assume center perturbations satisfy delta_0 <= a0 r/n and delta_{t+1} <= q delta_t + a r/n with q < 1, and margin density #{x: d2 - d1 <= h} <= mu n h. Then delta_t <= L_s r/n with L_s = a0 + a/(1-q), ideal certificate failures are at most 2 mu L_s r per round, and Phase-II work is O(nT + rdT + Ck log k T + [mu L_s r T + sum B_t + (n-r)|T_dir|](kd + k log k)).
theory.assumptions: A stable local basin (locally contractive guarded map, nondegenerate fair dual, well-separated means). These assumptions are not unconditional, and numerical-only failures B_t are not bounded.
theory.significance: Certificate failures scale with r rather than n only if replayed centers stay close to the cached ones. The paper explicitly declines to claim an unconditional speed theorem.

theory.name: Lemma 10 (Shared words need not give a stable categorical coupling)
theory.statement_plain: For the declared sampler (gcd reduction plus low-bit rejection sampling), two categorical calls with masses (m, m) and (m, m-1) that read the same random word select different categories with probability m/(2m-1) > 1/2, although their total-variation distance is only 1/[2(2m-1)].
theory.assumptions: FTF-1 sampler with ideal independent 64-bit words, both calls starting at the same word offset.
theory.significance: A tiny change in distribution does not mean a similar coupled sample under same-seed replay, so exact replay can be unstable.

theory.name: Proposition 11 (One legal deletion can force linear discarded work)
theory.statement_plain: Take a three-client, two-group 1-D dataset with n = 3m, k = 2 and gamma = T_a = 0, and one fixed legal single-record deletion. With probability at least (m-1)^2/(4m(2m-1)) > 1/16, every one of the 2m-1 retained group-A labels changes at round zero. Both certificate variants then abandon under the strict-majority rule, giving expected certificate failures and duplicated assignments of Omega(n).
theory.assumptions: Ideal random words; T >= 1; specific to the declared sampler, indexed cache and strict-majority fallback policy. It is not a universal lower bound and not a wall-clock claim.
theory.significance: A scoped obstruction showing that certification can cost more than it saves even for single deletions. This matches the empirical observation that certificates almost always abandon at round zero.

theory.name: Proposition 12 (Direct cache reconstruction upper bound)
theory.statement_plain: Rebuilding the per-point cache after a replay takes (n-r)kT center-point distance queries and O((n-r)kdT) arithmetic plus nearest/second selection.
theory.assumptions: Direct construction; this is an upper bound, not a lower bound.
theory.significance: Sequential record deletions with T > 0 are not free: the replay output invalidates the cache.

theory.name: Proposition 13 (Whole-client summary replay at initialization)
theory.statement_plain: For T = 0 and whole-client deletions that leave both groups nonempty, the following returns exactly fresh training's C(0): drop the departing clients' summaries, recompute the retained n'_g exactly, rebuild the canonical anchor list with weights h/n'_g, and rerun the server procedure from its original stream.
theory.assumptions: Local summaries depend only on their ordered slice, fixed parameters and a stream keyed by (s, c, g); trusted, unmodified compact state; persistent IDs, never renumbered.
theory.significance: A specialization of Theorem 5 that follows Pan et al. (2023, Sec 5.3, Alg 4); the authors say it is not a new general theorem. It enables a raw-data-free compact state (O(Ckd) coordinates plus O(C) counts) that survives sequential withdrawals by induction.

theory.name: Multi-group extension (Appendix B.4, Eqs 22-24)
theory.statement_plain: For m nonempty groups and gamma = 0, E Phi_m(C0) <= m alpha_k (sqrt(alpha_k) + 2)^2 Phi*_m. For gamma > 0 an additive O(m d gamma^2 log k) term appears.
theory.assumptions: Same as Theorem 1, with all m global groups nonempty.
theory.significance: Group separation still works for m > 2, but the linear dependence on m does not improve on the best known centralized multi-group results.

theory.name: Multi-group fixed-partition dual (Appendix G)
theory.statement_plain: For m > 2 groups and a fixed partition, the minimax center update is the convex epigraph program min theta s.t. f_g(C) <= theta. Its concave Lagrange dual over the simplex gives candidate centers b_j(lambda)/A_j(lambda). Any feasible tuple with max_g f_g(C) - D(lambda) <= eta is eta-optimal by weak duality.
theory.assumptions: Fixed partition; exactness of replay needs only a deterministic solver, not optimality.
theory.significance: Basis for the Frank-Wolfe multi-group prototype with certified duality gaps.

paper.complexity: Training communication: Phase I sends at most 2k anchors plus multiplicities per client (one shot). Phase II sends dense packets of 2k(d+2) numbers per client per round (not measured as bytes or network cost). Server initialization costs O(Ck^2(d + log k)(1 + T_a)) on at most 2Ck anchors. Each training round assigns all n points in O(n(kd + k log k)). Storage: the per-point cache is 64nT bytes in memory (48nT serialized), and the ACS checkpoints averaged 103 MB (max 504 MB; mean build 2.44 s). Replay cost (Eq 29) is O(W0 + W_I + nT + CkdT + Ck log k T + (L+2)kdT + rdT + [sum F_t + (n-r)|T_dir|](kd + k log k)). W0 = O(nd + nr + (n+r) log(n+r+2) + C) is setup, unavoidable even at T = 0. W_I = O(M_s(kd + k log k) + Q_s d + Ck + Ck^2(d + log k)(1+T_a)) covers touched slices and the server, and E[M_s] <= r s_max for random requests. Direct replay still scans every survivor each round, so for T > 0 it saves only the Phase-I share. Whole-client T = 0 compact replay needs no raw records: it keeps O(Ckd) summary coordinates plus O(C) counts (0.28-3.35 MB versus 12.5-55 MB full checkpoints) and per request reruns only the server sampler. Rebuilding the cache for sequential deletions costs (n-r)kT distance queries (Prop 12).

datasets: Synthetic 1-D lower-bound constructions (P1): kappa in {1, 2, ..., 128}, k = 1, 10,000 seeds per method/kappa
UCI Adult (P2): 30,162 records, 100 clients, d = 103, groups = male mask vs complement (9,782 / 20,380)
UCI Bank Marketing (P2): 45,211 records, 20 clients, d = 42, groups = married vs not (17,997 / 27,214)
UCI Default of Credit Card Clients 'Credit' (P2): 30,000 records, 100 clients, d = 23, groups = EDUCATION in {1,2} vs other (5,385 / 24,615)

2018 ACS 1-year PUMS person records (P3), 3,207,990 eligible records, 16 Folktables ACSEmployment features, SEX groups; clients = states (C = 10, 25, 50) or state-qualified PUMAs (C = 100, 250); n = 100k-1M; 19 one-factor configurations x 5 seeds = 95 trials
ACS 2018 with nine RAC1P race groups for the multi-group prototype (100,000 rows, 10 states, Missouri withdrawn)
models: Socially fair k-means centers (k = 2-64; k = 10 in budget/whole-client studies); no neural models
baselines: Fresh same-seed retraining on retained data (the exact-unlearning reference)
Direct replay, Basic-certificate replay, Runner-up-certificate replay (own variants)
Merged-1k and Merged-2k (locally balanced merged summaries adapted from Pan et al. 2023 / MUFC)
Ordinary Lloyd updates from identical fair-initialized centers (matched-start comparator)
metrics: Balanced sum G and expected approximation ratios G/G*, Phi/Phi*
Total fresh/replay algorithm-time ratio and end-to-end (E2E) time ratio; paired ratios; wins/losses
Resident request-time ratio for whole-client deletion
Certificate attempts A, passes P, useful saved S, duplicated J, useful coverage S/N
Exact equality of indexed centers and raw integer N, S, SS (replay vs fresh)
headline_results: Exactness: all 810 original replay comparisons (525 P2 + 285 P3) match fresh retraining exactly in every indexed center and raw integer statistic; all 135 record-budget, 90 whole-client positive-budget and compact-state comparisons also match.

Whole-client deletion (k = 10, one preselected client per dataset, 5 seeds): at T = 0, compact replay is 35.79x faster than fresh (Adult 26.96, Bank 115.53, Credit 25.03) and direct replay 17.79x. Canonical Direct is 2.357x at T = 1 (2.053/2.646/2.647) and 1.696x at T = 2 (1.544/1.828/1.856), winning all 15 cases at each budget. These are resident request-time ratios with inputs in memory, excluding cold load, network and persistence.
Quality price of T = 0: worst-group cost is 18.2-62.1% above two-round training (mean Phi T=0 to T=2: Adult 117.96 to 96.00, Bank 45.90 to 32.63, Credit 20.12 to 13.01).

Record deletion P2 (Adult/Bank/Credit, T = 15, r = 30/45/30): Direct total algorithm ratio 1.061 (E2E 1.049), beating retraining in 173/175 trials. Basic 1.006 (E2E 0.996); Runner-up 1.005 (E2E 0.995); useful certificate coverage 0.76%; certificates abandon at round zero in 174/175 trials.

Record deletion P3 (ACS, 95 trials): Direct 1.056 (E2E 1.043), wins 80/95; Basic 0.938 (E2E 0.930); Runner-up 0.940 (E2E 0.931); useful coverage 1.35%; abandonment at round zero in 92/95 trials. Only three r = 1 trials never fell back, reaching 14-17x algorithm ratios.

Record deletion with small budgets (k = 10): Direct algorithm ratios at T = 0/1/2 are 4.12/1.74/1.42 (Adult), 1.39/1.23/1.16 (Bank), 3.70/1.97/1.59 (Credit). Phi falls 19.8/31.2/29.0% from T = 0 to T = 2.
Heterogeneity P1 at kappa = 128: Merged-1k mean G/G* = 63.53 (SE 1.10) versus SplitGroup-2k 2.24, Merged-2k 1.90, centralized 1.77.
Fair vs ordinary Lloyd from identical initialization at T = 2: worst-group cost 3.2-5.1% lower, but population-average cost 0.5-4.7% higher, in all 30 cases.
Three sequential T = 0 withdrawals: fresh/compact 34.99x (matched outputs), 22.27x including buffered state round-trip.
Multi-group prototype (9 RAC1P groups): fresh/direct request ratios 138.70/1.60/1.30 at T = 0/1/2; compact T = 0 139.14; Phi 16.374/9.994/9.445.

limitations: Stated: exactness is conditional on one fixed represented dataset and preprocessing state; it does not erase a record's influence on the fitted scaler, encoding or vocabulary.

Stated: refined batch outputs invalidate the per-point cache, so further record replay needs cache reconstruction ((n-r)kT distance queries). Only the T = 0 whole-client compact state supports cheap sequential deletion.
Stated: the canonical learner and main experiments are binary-group; multi-group is only a separate prototype tested on one population and one request.

Stated: timings come from a local single-machine simulation (Apple M3 Max, warm OS caches, nondedicated desktop, five seeds). Network, secure aggregation, stragglers, dropouts, durable persistence and physical purge are unmeasured.
Stated: federation is not differential privacy or cryptographic erasure. Group anchors (which can coincide with records at gamma = 0) and small group-cell changes can leak information.
Stated: group-average squared cost does not establish individual, intersectional, representation or downstream fairness, and fair updates raise population-average cost.

Stated: there is no fresh-independent distributional guarantee for deletion requests chosen adaptively from the seed-dependent checkpoint, and no equality of full internal state. Requests that empty a group are excluded.
Stated: the deletion settings where reuse pays most (whole client, T = 0) are the ones with worse fairness quality (worst-group cost 18-62% higher than T = 2).

Noticed: per-record gains are tiny (about 6% algorithm time). Certificates almost never pay off (useful coverage under 1.4%, abandonment at round zero in 174/175 and 92/95 trials) and increase aggregate E2E cost.
Noticed: for T > 0, replay still scans all survivors each round (O(n) per round). No sublinear exact replay for refinement is offered, so savings come only from Phase-I reuse.

Noticed: the headline 35.8x uses a separate compact implementation with 3 timing repeats, while the T = 1/2 ratios use canonical Direct with 4 repeats. The whole-client evidence uses one preselected client per dataset (two in K.2), and Bank's 115x reflects having only 20 clients / 380 anchor slots.

Noticed: the whole-client T = 0 path is essentially MUFC's server-only retraining with demographic reweighting (the authors say so). The new theory is mostly about initialization quality and replay exactness, not asymptotic deletion-time bounds like Ginart et al. or MUFC.

Noticed: exactness depends on bit-exact engineering (fixed-point encoding, exact rational sampling, canonical ordering). An implementation detail (pickle-restored array descriptors) changed a feature-sum reduction speed by 5-6x, which shows how fragile timing comparisons are.

Noticed: Adult/Credit raw-data provenance is incomplete (processed inputs only). An initial reporting error swapped Phi and G (corrected in App J.1). The authors also report using generative AI extensively, including for proofs (partially Lean-checked).
future_work: Implied: make the multi-group (m > 2) map canonical, with exact or certified fair updates, beyond the bounded Frank-Wolfe prototype.
Implied: measure networked deployments with secure aggregation, stragglers, dropouts, durable state and physical purge.
Implied: support sequential deletions at positive refinement budgets (cache maintenance or reconstruction) and longer or adaptive request sequences.
Implied: richer caches (e.g. Yinyang/Elkan-style bounds) or more stable samplers that let certification cover more work.
Implied: distributional guarantees for adaptively chosen requests (Ullah-Arora model-and-state targets).
paper.relevance_to_efficient_unlearning: This is the graph's most direct bridge between MUFC-style federated clustering unlearning, Ginart-style exact deletion, and fairness. Its key design lesson for efficient exact unlearning is to keep cached summaries independent of any global normalization (here 1/n_g), so a deletion only changes cheap server-side reweighting and never invalidates untouched work, much like SISA's untouched shards. It provides reusable proof tools: a slice-wise D^2-sampling plus Minkowski composition argument for proportion-independent guarantees, an induction showing that exact signed patches of additive statistics reproduce retraining, and certificate soundness and tightness results. It is also an honest negative result: exact replay alone saves little when later iterative rounds must rescan all data, and same-seed D^2 sampling is discontinuous, so a single deletion can force Omega(n) wasted work under the studied policy. For a student this sets a concrete benchmark to beat: per-record exact unlearning for federated (fair) k-means with T > 0 that is clearly faster than 1.06x retraining.
open_questions: Design a deletion-stable seeded sampler for D^2/k-means++ seeding, such as per-record persistent exponential/Gumbel keys or priority sampling, whose selections rarely change when one record is deleted. It must keep same-seed exactness and avoid the Lemma 10/Prop 11 instability so that certificates actually save work.

Achieve sublinear exact replay for T > 0 refinement rounds by combining group-cell statistics with DC-k-means-style hierarchical partitions or SISA-style slicing of refinement, and analyze the quality vs deletion-time trade-off with an amortized bound.

Give a deletion-time analysis of the expected per-record unlearning cost for SplitGroup-2k (in the style of MUFC's Theorem 5.4 or Ginart's amortized bounds), since the paper gives only work bounds and conditional stability results.

Integrate secure aggregation (e.g. MUFC's SCMA) and privacy for group-separated summaries. Group anchors reveal group membership and can equal raw records at gamma = 0, so measure the communication and leakage costs of exact replay.

Extend exact replay to multi-group and intersectional fairness with an exact or certified fair update and per-group guarantees, testing whether replay stays efficient as m grows (the bound degrades linearly in m).

Combine demographic social fairness with client-level fairness (as in p-FClus, MFC or FedShard's efficiency fairness) under unlearning: when one client withdraws, can both group costs and client costs and burdens stay balanced?
Compare exact replay with approximate or certified unlearning for fair federated clustering (e.g. (eps, delta)-indistinguishable deletions), including guarantees for adaptively chosen requests.

nodes.label: Machine unlearning
nodes.description: Removing the influence of specific training data from a trained model, ideally so the result matches a model trained without that data.

nodes.label: Exact unlearning
nodes.description: Unlearning whose output is identical, or identically distributed, to retraining from scratch on the retained data.

nodes.label: Federated unlearning
nodes.description: Unlearning in federated systems, where data stays at clients and deletion requests may concern single records or entire clients.

nodes.label: Federated clustering
nodes.description: Learning shared cluster centers from data distributed across clients without pooling raw records, usually from local summaries or aggregated statistics.

nodes.label: K-means clustering
nodes.description: Partitioning points into k clusters by choosing k centers that minimize the sum of squared distances from each point to its nearest center.

nodes.label: Fair clustering (group-fair)
nodes.description: Clustering formulations that add fairness requirements with respect to protected demographic groups, such as balanced representation in clusters or equitable group costs.

nodes.label: Fairness of machine unlearning
nodes.description: Study of how data deletion interacts with fairness, and of unlearning methods that preserve or account for group fairness.

nodes.label: Right to be forgotten
nodes.description: Legal right, e.g. GDPR Article 17, for individuals to request erasure of their personal data; a main motivation for machine unlearning.

nodes.label: Client fairness
nodes.description: Fairness notion in federated learning that asks for equitable cost, accuracy or burden across participating clients rather than across demographic groups.

nodes.label: Client-level (whole-client) unlearning
nodes.description: Federated unlearning where an entire client or institution withdraws and all of its data must be removed from the trained model.

nodes.label: k-means++
nodes.description: Seeding for k-means that picks the first center uniformly and each next center with probability proportional to its squared distance to the nearest chosen center (D^2 sampling); O(log k)-approximate in expectation.

nodes.label: Weighted k-means++
nodes.description: k-means++ D^2 sampling over weighted points, where selection probability is proportional to weight times squared distance; used to cluster weighted summaries or representatives.

nodes.label: Lloyd's algorithm
nodes.description: Iterative k-means heuristic that alternates nearest-center assignment with recomputing each center as the mean of its cluster.

nodes.label: Retrain from scratch
nodes.description: Baseline unlearning that retrains the model on the retained data; the reference for exact unlearning but usually expensive.

nodes.label: Quantized k-means (Q-k-means)
nodes.description: Deletion-efficient k-means (Ginart et al., 2019) that quantizes centroids at each Lloyd iteration so that most deletions leave the quantized trajectory unchanged and need no retraining.

nodes.label: DC-k-means (DC-KM)
nodes.description: Divide-and-conquer k-means (Ginart et al., 2019) that clusters data subsets in a tree and, on deletion, recomputes only the tree path containing the deleted point.

nodes.label: k-FED
nodes.description: One-shot federated clustering (Dennis et al., 2021) in which each client runs local clustering, sends its local centers once, and the server clusters the collected centers.

nodes.label: Unlearning via k-means++ initialization
nodes.description: MUFC's unlearning approach: clients' k-means++ seeding summaries are reused and only affected parts are resampled. When a client is removed, only the server-side clustering is recomputed.

nodes.label: Quantization
nodes.description: Mapping continuous values to a discrete grid; in clustering unlearning it stabilizes centers or summaries against small data changes and reduces message size.

nodes.label: Batch unlearning
nodes.description: Processing a set of deletion requests together in a single unlearning operation rather than one at a time.

nodes.label: MUFSC (exact unlearning for federated socially fair k-means)
nodes.description: Federated socially fair k-means framework with exact same-seed replay unlearning. It combines group-separated local summaries, server-side global group normalization, guarded fair refinement on exact sufficient statistics, and replay that reuses untouched computation.

nodes.label: SplitGroup-2k (group-separated initialization)
nodes.description: Federated initialization in which each (client, group) ownership slice independently picks up to k representatives by local D^2 sampling and sends quantized anchors with multiplicities, so a client sends at most 2k anchors for two groups. The server then reweights the anchors and runs weighted D^2 sampling.

nodes.label: Server-side global group normalization (h/n_g)
nodes.description: Weighting each summary anchor by its multiplicity divided by the global size of its demographic group. Done only at the server, it is the single step that uses global group sizes.

nodes.label: GuardedFairUpdate_L
nodes.description: Deterministic two-group socially fair center update. It evaluates candidates on the Lagrangian curve between the group means (endpoints plus L bisection midpoints) from exact statistics, picks the lowest worst-group cost, and accepts it only if that cost is no higher than the current centers'.

nodes.label: Fair-Lloyd (Ghadiri et al. 2021)
nodes.description: Lloyd-style algorithm for socially fair k-means whose center step moves each center along the segment between its per-group means to minimize the maximum group-average cost.

nodes.label: Count-sum-squared-sum statistics (N, S, SS)
nodes.description: Additive sufficient statistics of a point set (count, vector sum, scalar squared-norm sum). They determine its mean and squared-error cost for any center and can be updated by adding or subtracting points.

nodes.label: Fixed-point encoding with exact integer accumulation
nodes.description: Encoding data once on a fixed-point grid (x = m * 2^-b) and accumulating statistics in exact integer arithmetic, so that subtracting a record's contribution exactly undoes adding it.

nodes.label: Per-entity keyed random streams
nodes.description: Giving every randomized entity (e.g. each data slice and the server) its own pseudorandom stream keyed by the seed and the entity identity, together with a fully specified exact categorical sampler. Entities whose inputs are unchanged then make identical draws on replay.

nodes.label: Same-seed exact batch replay (Algorithm 1)
nodes.description: Unlearning that replays the declared training procedure with the same seed on the retained data, reusing untouched summaries and patching cached statistics with exact signed corrections, so that it outputs exactly the retrained model.

nodes.label: Direct replay
nodes.description: Replay variant that reuses untouched initialization summaries but recomputes every retained record's nearest-center assignment in every refinement round, without certificates.

nodes.label: Assignment certificate (all-competitor / basic)
nodes.description: Test that uses a point's cached nearest and second-nearest distances and the centers' displacements (triangle-inequality movement bounds as in Elkan/Hamerly k-means acceleration) to prove its cached nearest center is unchanged. Points that fail are reassigned exactly.

nodes.label: Runner-up certificate
nodes.description: Stronger constant-time assignment certificate that also uses the cached runner-up center's identity and exact displacement: d1 + delta_j < min{|d2 - delta_r|, max(0, d2 - max over other centers of delta_m)}.

nodes.label: Compact whole-client replay (T = 0)
nodes.description: Raw-data-free whole-client unlearning for an initialization-only model. It stores per-client summaries and exact group counts; on withdrawal it drops the client's summaries, recomputes group sizes and weights, and reruns the server sampler from its original seed.

nodes.label: Merged-1k (locally balanced merged summary)
nodes.description: Single-summary federated initialization in which each client balances its demographic groups locally, runs one weighted D^2 sampling call, and sends at most k merged representatives weighted by global point weights.

nodes.label: Merged-2k
nodes.description: Merged-summary variant with local budget min(2k, n_c) that matches a group-separated method's anchor-slot count per client.

nodes.label: Multi-group Frank-Wolfe prototype (m > 2)
nodes.description: Multi-group socially fair implementation that indexes summaries and statistics by group and solves each fixed-partition update by bounded Frank-Wolfe search on the concave Lagrange dual, with an exact objective guard and a duality-gap certificate.

nodes.label: Unlearning cost
nodes.description: Computational, communication and storage cost of carrying out deletion requests, usually compared to retraining from scratch.

nodes.label: Unfairness
nodes.description: Systematic disparity in model quality or outcomes across demographic groups or clients.

nodes.label: Data heterogeneity (non-IID)
nodes.description: Non-identical data distributions across clients, including different shares of demographic groups at different sites.

nodes.label: Privacy leakage
nodes.description: Unintended disclosure of information about individual records through shared summaries, model outputs or retained state.

nodes.label: Adversarial deletion requests
nodes.description: Deletion requests chosen adaptively or adversarially, e.g. based on the released model, which can defeat average-case efficiency or distributional unlearning guarantees.

nodes.label: Accuracy-fairness trade-off
nodes.description: Improving outcomes for a disadvantaged group typically worsens overall or average performance.

nodes.label: Deletion-efficiency vs statistical-performance trade-off
nodes.description: Tension between how cheaply a model can process deletions and the statistical quality of the model.

nodes.label: Deletion-induced global reweighting
nodes.description: In objectives normalized by global group sizes, deleting one record changes the weight of every remaining record of its group at every site. A local deletion therefore has global effects and can invalidate otherwise untouched work.

nodes.label: Floating-point non-invertibility of aggregates
nodes.description: Floating-point sums are not invertible: subtracting a deleted contribution from a rounded aggregate need not equal a fresh sum over the retained data, which breaks exact incremental updates.

nodes.label: Seeded sampling instability under deletion
nodes.description: Sequential seeded sampling such as D^2 sampling is discontinuous. A tiny change in sampling masses can change the selected items under the same random words, cascading into different centers and assignments.

nodes.label: Stale cache after replay
nodes.description: After an exact replay, per-point caches (labels, distances) still describe the old trajectory, so further sequential deletions need costly cache reconstruction.

nodes.label: Exact deletion: same distribution as retraining
nodes.description: Formal exact deletion criterion: the unlearned model must have the same distribution as the model trained from scratch on the data without the deleted points.

nodes.label: Unlearning guarantee
nodes.description: A formal statement that an unlearning procedure meets a deletion criterion, either exact equality with retraining or bounded indistinguishability.

nodes.label: Approximation guarantee
nodes.description: Bound on how far an algorithm's objective can be from the optimum, typically as a multiplicative factor in expectation.

nodes.label: k-means++ O(log k) approximation
nodes.description: k-means++ seeding is O(log k)-competitive in expectation; Arthur and Vassilvitskii give factor 8(ln k + 2), improved to 5(ln k + 2) by Makarychev, Reddy and Shan (2020).

nodes.label: Exactness of k-means++ seeding unlearning (Lemma 5.1)
nodes.description: MUFC's result that unlearning by reusing k-means++ seeding and resampling only when affected yields the same output distribution as retraining.

nodes.label: Socially fair k-means objective
nodes.description: Clustering objective that minimizes the maximum over demographic groups of the group-average squared distance to the nearest center: Phi(C) = max_g (1/n_g) sum over x in group g of min_j ||x - c_j||^2. Each record is effectively weighted by 1/n_g.

nodes.label: Same-seed exact unlearning (declared training map)
nodes.description: Exactness defined relative to a fully specified randomized training procedure: for every seed, the unlearning output equals retraining on the retained data with that same seed. Equality in distribution follows for requests chosen independently of the seed.

nodes.label: Model-output vs model-and-state exactness targets
nodes.description: Distinction (Ullah et al., 2021; Ullah and Arora, 2023) between exact unlearning of only the released model or trajectory and of the full internal model-and-state. It also separates fixed from adaptively chosen deletion requests.

nodes.label: Local/global group-share mismatch kappa
nodes.description: Heterogeneity parameter equal to the largest ratio, over mixed clients, between a client's shares of the two global groups (n_{c,A}/n_A vs n_{c,B}/n_B). It measures how much local group balancing distorts global group weights.

nodes.label: SplitGroup-2k warm-start guarantee (Thm 1)
nodes.description: Under ideal sampling, group-separated federated D^2 initialization satisfies E[Phi] <= 2 alpha_k (sqrt(alpha_k)+2)^2 Phi* (O(log^2 k)) at zero quantization, independent of n, number of clients, group imbalance and client group proportions.

nodes.label: Merged-1k Theta(kappa) heterogeneity loss (Thm 2)
nodes.description: A locally group-balanced merged summary has expected G/G* = O(kappa log^2 k). This is tight: instances exist with ratio at least kappa/2 for G and kappa/4 for Phi.

nodes.label: Matched-slot initialization gap (Prop 7)
nodes.description: On a three-location instance with equal anchor-slot budgets, Merged-2k has expected G/G* = (kappa+5)/3 and Phi/Phi* = (kappa+8)/6, versus 2 and 3/2 for SplitGroup-2k. One fair refinement round removes the gap.

nodes.label: Guarded fair update monotonicity (Prop 3)
nodes.description: Nearest-center reassignment followed by a guarded fair center update never increases the worst-group cost. Without the guard, finite bisection can increase it.

nodes.label: All-competitor certificate lemma (Lemma 4, Prop 8)
nodes.description: A cached nearest center j stays uniquely nearest if delta_j + max_{m != j} delta_m < d2 - d1. Given only (j, d1, d2) and displacement radii this is the strongest sound test; a runner-up identity allows a strictly stronger O(1) test.

nodes.label: Seeded exact batch replay theorem (Thm 5)
nodes.description: With exact additive statistics, deterministic arithmetic and tie rules, per-slice and server seeded streams, sound certificates and a valid batch, same-seed replay reproduces retraining's entire indexed center trajectory and final model for every seed.

nodes.label: Replay work bound and locally stable replay (Eq 29, Prop 9)
nodes.description: Unit-cost work bound for replay: setup + touched-slice and server re-initialization + per-round survivor scans + (failed certificates + direct rounds) x assignment cost. Under contraction and margin-density assumptions, certificate failures scale with the deletion size r.

nodes.label: Shared-word coupling instability (Lemma 10)
nodes.description: Two nearly identical categorical laws (total-variation distance 1/[2(2m-1)]) sampled with the same random word by a gcd-reduced rejection sampler can disagree with probability m/(2m-1) > 1/2.

nodes.label: One deletion forces linear discarded work (Prop 11)
nodes.description: For a specific three-client instance and the declared sampler, cache and strict-majority fallback, one legal record deletion flips all retained group-A labels with probability > 1/16. This forces Omega(n) expected certificate failures and duplicated assignments.

nodes.label: Whole-client summary replay exactness (Prop 13)
nodes.description: For an initialization-only model, dropping withdrawn clients' summaries, recomputing group counts and weights, and rerunning the server sampler from its original stream exactly reproduces fresh training on the surviving clients.

nodes.label: Multi-group warm-start bound (App B.4)
nodes.description: Extension of the group-separated initialization guarantee to m groups: E[Phi_m] <= m alpha_k (sqrt(alpha_k)+2)^2 Phi*_m at zero quantization, with an additive O(m d gamma^2 log k) term otherwise.

nodes.label: Worst-group cost (Phi)
nodes.description: Maximum over demographic groups of the group-average squared distance to the nearest center, i.e. the socially fair k-means objective value; lower means the worst-served group is served better.

nodes.label: K-means cost
nodes.description: Sum or average of squared distances from points to their nearest centers.

nodes.label: Speedup
nodes.description: Ratio of a baseline's (e.g. retraining's) time to the method's time for the same task.

nodes.label: End-to-end (E2E) request time
nodes.description: Wall-clock time of a deletion request including input materialization, checkpoint loading and output writing, not only the core algorithm call.

nodes.label: Useful certificate coverage (S/N)
nodes.description: Fraction of eligible survivor point-rounds whose assignment work a certificate actually saved, after discarding passes undone by fallback.

nodes.label: Approximation ratio (G/G*, Phi/Phi*)
nodes.description: Ratio of an algorithm's (expected) objective value to the optimal objective value on the same instance.

nodes.label: UCI Adult
nodes.description: UCI Adult census-income tabular dataset with demographic attributes, widely used in fairness research.

nodes.label: UCI Bank Marketing
nodes.description: UCI dataset of direct-marketing campaigns of a Portuguese bank, with client demographic and campaign features.

nodes.label: UCI Default of Credit Card Clients
nodes.description: Tabular dataset of 30,000 Taiwanese credit-card clients (Yeh and Lien, 2009) with demographic, credit-limit and payment-history features.

nodes.label: 2018 ACS PUMS (Folktables)
nodes.description: 2018 American Community Survey 1-year Public Use Microdata Sample person records from the US Census Bureau, commonly accessed via Folktables schemas such as ACSEmployment.

nodes.label: Synthetic heterogeneity lower-bound instances
nodes.description: Small synthetic one-dimensional constructions (few clients and locations) built to realize a chosen local/global group-share mismatch kappa and test initialization lower bounds.

cross_paper.note: MUFC (with shared co-author Saurav Prakash) is the closest precedent. Its two-level k-means++ seeding/server clustering, secure aggregation and server-only retraining after client removal (Sec 5.3, Alg 4) are reused; the T=0 whole-client result (Prop 13) is explicitly a specialization, not a new theorem. New here: group-separated summaries with global demographic normalization, exact replay of fair refinement rounds, and showing that MUFC's single-summary design adapted to the fair objective (Merged-1k) loses Theta(kappa). MUFC's reported 84x is called not directly comparable.

Both study exact deletion for k-means. Ginart's Q-k-means (quantized centroids, stability tests) and DC-k-means (recompute affected tree paths) are cited as centralized precedents of the certificate-based stability checks and touched-slice reuse; this paper moves to federated socially fair k-means and same-seed pointwise exactness.

SISA's sharded retraining is cited only as a different deletion procedure. Conceptually, reusing untouched (client, group) slice summaries and recomputing touched ones mirrors SISA's untouched shards, but nothing is ensembled and the output equals full retraining.

FedShard is cited as addressing client efficiency/performance fairness in federated unlearning. This paper's fairness is a demographic worst-group clustering cost and explicitly claims nothing about fair client computation burdens.

p-FClus is not cited (the cited 'Gupta et al., 2025' is a different ARCANE k-means++ exact cluster unlearning paper). p-FClus equalizes per-client clustering cost, whereas this paper equalizes demographic group-average cost across clients and adds exact unlearning.

MFC is not cited. Both are federated k-means with client summaries and multiple rounds. MFC targets client-level cost fairness and heterogeneity without deletion; this paper targets demographic social fairness plus exact replay unlearning.

Not cited, but both study fairness and exact unlearning together. FairSISA post-processes a SISA ensemble for supervised group fairness; this paper builds the fair objective into federated clustering and keeps exact replay. Both cite Oesterling et al.'s fair machine unlearning.
